Q: How can I use Symfony AssetMapper with npm packages installed in the root node_modules? A:

When using Symfony AssetMapper with npm packages, you can keep all npm packages in root /node_modules and selectively register the subfolders containing the package entry points for AssetMapper.

Workflow example:

1️⃣ Register the folders in AssetMapper

framework:
    asset_mapper:
        # The paths to make available to the asset mapper.
        paths:
            assets/ : ''
            node_modules/@hpcc-js/wasm/dist/ :  'hpcc'

Here the folder node_modules/@hpcc-js/wasm/dist/ has been registered with the namespace hpcc. You should define a namespace for each of the registered folders. The problem is that every asset is identified relative to its registered folder. If you have index.js in two registered folders, only one of them will be identified.

2️⃣ Require the package in importmap

bin/console importmap:require @hpcc-js/wasm --path=./node_modules/@hpcc-js/wasm/dist/index.js
  • This creates a mapping in the importmap that tells the browser where to find @hpcc-js/wasm.

3️⃣ Clear Symfony cache

bin/console cache:clear

4️⃣ Use the package in the browser

import { Graphviz } from "@hpcc-js/wasm";

const gv = new Graphviz();
gv.layout("digraph { a -> b }", "svg").then(svg => {
  document.body.innerHTML = svg;
});

Key points:

  • Only the registered folders are served by AssetMapper.
  • All relative imports inside the registered folders work automatically.
  • Root node_modules is still available for Node/Vite tooling.
  • Registered folders must include all dependencies that the package imports in the browser.

5️⃣ Alternative approach

Some users create a postinstall script in package.json to copy necessary files from root node_modules into assets/vendor, for example:

"postinstall": "cp -R node_modules/@organization assets/vendor/@organization"

This can be useful if you want to expose only specific files instead of an entire folder. However, it duplicates files and requires maintenance whenever packages are updated. Note that AssetMapper only serves the files in the registered folders that are needed for browser imports.

In most cases — including @hccp-js/wasm, where the entire dist directory is intended for the browser — registering the relevant folder with AssetMapper is cleaner, avoids duplication, and automatically resolves relative imports.

Reference: For more details and discussion, see the Symfony issue: https://github.com/symfony/symfony-docs/issues/22000

Q: Python Regex for a closing parenthesis without an opening parenthesis A:

I think there are multiple things here:

(1) your regex doesn't do what you say it does, because of the start/end anchors and whitespace. Your regex would only match a string like " (", so much more narrow than what you claim to be able to match with it on regex101. So something is not the same between your local environment and regex101, I tested if this is about multiline-mode or maybe re.search vs re.match but nothing really works. I think the difference must be in your actual regex or test-string.

(2) Your problem is not really suitable for regex. For the simple case of one open bracket without a closing bracket, you can indeed use regex. Other answers have attempts. You can tell they are already a bit complex. And they will totally fall apart when presented with something like "(()". This is because bracket-closing is a Type 2 (context-free) language and not a Type 3 (regular) language. See Chomsky-Hierarchy if this classification is new to you. You usually deal with context-free and regular languages, understand the difference between the two and you will know what regex can and can't do. *

Fortunately, for this simple case, you only need a very simple degenerate case of a push-down automaton. Normally, you need to take care of a stack, but in this case, a counter is enough. Go through the characters one by one with a counter cnt on how many open brackets you have seen so far. Decrement it for a closing bracket. If you ever decrement it below 0, you have a superfluous closing bracket. If you reach the end of the string and the counter is not zero, you have a superfluous opening bracket.


def has_valid_parens(s: str):
    cnt = 0
    for c in s:
        if c == "(":
            cnt += 1
        elif c == ")":
            cnt -= 1
            if cnt < 0:
                return False # closing bracket when none was opened
    return cnt == 0 # true if all brackets closed

This will work correctly even on things like "()()", "((())" and trivially ignore all non-bracket characters.

* actually, regex-libraries including python re, usually do a bit more than what a theoretical computer scientist calls a 'regex', but the limitations are similar.

Q: How do I parse ndjson files? A:

Fixed it by adding in the following header to the request.

headers = {
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}', # Need this or you will get a 401: Not Authorized response
    'Accept': 'application/x-ndjson'
}

After this I convert the ndjson by:

resp_json = []
ndjson = response.content.decode().split('\n')

for json_obj in ndjson:
    if json_obj:
        resp_json.append(json.loads(json_obj))

Now you will have your parsable object.

Q: How to switch namespace in kubernetes A:

I like my answers short, to the point and with references to official documentation:

Answer:

This is the command, but please consider that it will edit your kubeconfig file

kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=my-namespace

From:

https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/cheatsheet/
